column3: Pick up your rental car and explore the historic centers of Split and Trogir.
Dining: Visit Pandora Greenbox in Split for its highly-rated plant-based menu.
Take the car ferry from Split to Vela Luka (approx. 3 hours).
Explore Korčula Town, known as "Little Dubrovnik" for its medieval charm.
Drive to Lumbarda to experience the only sandy beach on the island, Vela Pržina.
Take the 20-minute car ferry from Korčula (Dominče) to Orebić.
Stay: Consider basing yourself in Orebić at a place like Aminess Bellevue Village for beach access, or find a quiet guesthouse in the village of Dingac-Potocine for a more remote feel.
Beaches: Spend a day at Trstenica Beach in Orebić, which features fine sand and pebbles. For more seclusion, drive to Divna Beach or Duba Beach on the northern shores.
Wine: Tour the world-renowned Dingač wine-growing hills. Matusko winery is a highly recommended stop (booking required, cash only).
Dining: "Dalmatinac" in Orebić offers vegan pizza and a significant array of vegetarian dishes.
Drive south toward Dubrovnik with a stop in Ston to see the ancient defensive walls.
Relax at Prapratno Beach, a popular sandy spot near Ston with crystal-clear, shallow water.
Continue the scenic drive to Dubrovnik (approx. 1 hour from Ston).
